rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTIONALIZ E THE USE OF ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES AND TO INCORPORATE THE PHILIPPINE CENTER FOR ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The term "ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION SYSTEM" means any process or procedure used to resolve a dispute or controversy, other than by adjudication of a presiding judge of a court or an officer of a government agency, as defined in this Act, in which a naeutral third party participates to assist in the resoultion of issues, which includes arbitration, mediation, conciliation, early neutral evaluation, mini-trial, or any combination thereof.> This bill is the solution to the problem of the almost one million cases presntly jamming the lowest to the highest courts, which has een a major impediment to Philippine democracy.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05654

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL FORMS OF SMUGGLING AS ECONOMIC SABOTAGE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: Economic sabotage means any act or activity which undermines, weakens or renders into disrepute the economic system or viability of the country or tends to bring about such effects to include, but not necessarily limited to, the following offenses:trafficking, all forms of smuggling including technical smuggling, counterfeiting, blackmarketing or mass movement of local or foreign currency in violation of existing laws and regulations, price manipulation to the prejudice of the public especially in the sale of prime commodities in violation of price control laws, tax evasion, bank swindling and violation of land reform laws. > The gravity of the effects of all forms of smuggling has gone bad to worse. the losses in revenue and tax collectiion cannot anymore be ignored. Smuggling must now be considered as form of economic sabotage because of its effects on the economy.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PRIVILEGES GRANTED TO SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 4 (a) & (b) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, ENTITLED `AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION-BUILDING , GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to increase the discount privileges from twenty percent (10%) to forty percent (40%), It is the purpose of this important legilsative measure to help our senior citizens to fight the economic difficulties in our midst in order to survive. They have no more place to turn to because even if they are willing to work to sustain their needs, their age and health conditions certainly will discourage people to hire them. The goverment therefore, has to provide alternatives to rescue these people from extreme difficulties as concrete gesture of gratitude to them for the services they had contributed during their most productive years.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to oblige multinational and domestic manufacturing corporations to allocate one percent (1%) of their net annual corporate income for scientific and technological R & D activities. It likewsie hopes that by giving momentum to R & D activities, we will ensure sustained economic growth.

rows.abstract: Section 63 of RA No. 7160, the Local Government Code, as amended to read as follows: >Any abuse of the exercise of the power of preventive suspension shall be penalized as abuse of authority. PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT LOCAL OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES WHOFAIL TO COMPLY WITH DECISIONS, ORDERS, OR RULINGS OF THE CONCERNED LOCAL SANGGUNIANG BODY, EXCEPT SANGGUNIANG BARANGAY, IN THE EXERCISE OF ITS DISCIPLINARY FUNCTIONS OVER ELECTIVE LOCAL OFFICIALS, AND ANY PERSON WHO REFUSES TO COMPLY WITH ANY OF ITSLAWFUL ORDERS IN CONNECTION THEREAT SHALL BE LIABLE FOR CONTEMPT OF SUCH LEGISLATIVE BODT." > Another paragaraph is all added, and shall read as follows: >" THE LOCAL SANGGUNIANG BODIES SHALL HAVE THE POWER TO ISSUE SUBPOENA AD TESTIFICANDUM AND SUBBPOENA DUCES TECUM FOR THE PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS AND RECRODS PERTINENT TO INVESTIGATIONS AND INQUIRIES CONDUCTED BY THEM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THEIR AUTHORITY TO DISCIPLINE LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICIALS."

rows.abstract: "LENDING COMPAY REGULATION ACT OF 2001." Rationale: The upsurge of Lending Company  (LCs) is expected to continue unabated as evidence by the continuous registration of new LCs with Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) and some Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFI) is converting into LCs. this may be partly attributed to the relatively free and unregulated operational NBFIs. Common complaints on LCs cover high lending rates, non0disclosure of all charges on loans and non-issuance of official receipts. > In view of their growth in numbers and the significant LCs have in the economic activities of the general public, the enactment of a law that would regulate their establishment and operations appears imperative.

And while hundreds of millions of pesos worth of goods have been intercepted and confiscated , smuggling is such a lucrative practice that the influx  of smuggled products remain unabated. > The Philippines does not have the means and resources to stem the tide and the national government has been criticized for its lack of political will in implementing harsher penalties andstringent measures to curb this practice. The siutation in effect condones smuggling and therefore must be rectified.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FISCAL AUTONOMY TO ALL WATER DISTRICTS AND INCREASING THE MEMBERSHIP ON THEIR BOARD OF DIRECTORS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE `PROVINCIAL WATER UTILITIES ACT OF 1973,' AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The establishment of water districts has considerably improved the water supply at reasonable rates in urban and rural areas. However, the water district is guided by restrictive fiscal polices, rules and regulations which hinder initiatives and innovations and restrict its organizational and operational flexibility. Such situation makes it difficult for a water district to fully mobilize its resources and capabilities and maximize its potentials toward contributing to the attainmentof sustainable growth and development. > Cognizant of these restraints, there is therefore a need to grant fiscal autonomy in the operation, financial affairs and transactions of the district. This would mean autonomy in the programming, administeriing and managing of its own budget and other resources with the wisdom and dispatch that their needs require.

rows.abstract: "National Environmental Management Authority (NEMA) Act." Rationale: Environmental problems in the Philippines are multi-faceted forest denudation, destruction of marine life, loss of soil fertility, urban air and water pollution, and inadequate wastes disposal systems are environmental problems that rob us and the future generations of a clean and health environment.> This bill therefore, proposes the creation of the National Environmental Management Authority (NEMA), an environmental watchdogwhich shall be responsible for the conservation of the country's environemnt and resources, regulation of environmental impact occasioned by human activities, and control and abatement of environmental pollution.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE VOTER'S REGISTRATION ACT OF 1996' TO PROVIDE FOR THE HOLDING OF PERIODIC GENERAL VOTERS' REGISTRATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The continuing system of voter's registration established by R.A. No. 8189, otherwise known as the Voter's Registration Act of 1996, has spawned the massive and widespread disenfranchisem ent of legitimate voters as demonstrated in regular and special elections held since the enactment of the law. Unless remedied, the situation could erode the people's faith in the electoral process and thus weaken the strongest pillar of our democratic system of goverment. > The bill seeks to provide that remedy by requiring that a general registration of voters be conducted by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) periodically but only prior to a presidential election rather than before any regular or special election.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to increase the number of branches of (a) the Regional Trial Courts in all the judicial regions; (b) the Metropolitan Trial Courts in the National Judicial Region; and (c) the Municipal Trial Courts in certain cities and municipalities. The bill has the following other salient features: (1) The bill allots at least one Regional Trial Court for every city; and (2) It likewise provides for Municipal Trial Courts in newly-created cities, and additional branches of the Regional Trial Courts, Metropolitan Trial Courts and Municipal Trial Courts in the different cities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ELEVATING THE RANK OF THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS (CTA) TO THE LEVEL OF A COLLEGIATE COURT WITH SPECIAL JURISDICTION, ENLARGING ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, EXPANDING ITS JURISDICTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF THE LAW CREATING THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Presently, the jurisdiction over criminal cases involving violations of the tax and customs laws is lodged with the regular courts, while the civil aspect of these cases is with the Court of Tax Appeals, thus resulting into needless delays in the final disposition of cases. Also, collection cases before the regular courts remain unattended in view of their large caseload. With respect to local tax and real property cases, there is no definite jurisprudence other than decisions of theSupreme Court, which are few and far between, on the matter. > In view of the foregoing and for a better administration of our revenue laws, this bill seeks to amend and revised Republic Act No. 1125 giving the Court of Tax Appeals criminal jurisdicction over tax and customs cases, jurisdiction over collection cases increasing its membership, expanding its organizational set up, and raising its level to that of the Court of Tax Appeals.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06673

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF TOURISM OFFICER IN ALL PROVINCES, FIRST CLASS MUNICIPALITIES AND CITIES, OR MUNICIPALITIES AND CITIES WHERE TOURISMS IS CONSIDERED A MAJOR LOCAL INDUSTRY, AND DEFINING ITS QUALIFICATIONS, POWER AND DUTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE
rows.abstract: Among the major problems affecting the tourism industry is accessibility to basic tourism information and services and lack of a comprehensive approach to its development, resulting in low tourist arrival. In 1999, the Philippines ranked fifth amongASEAN members in terms of visitor arrivals with 2.2. million tourists. It lagged behind Thailand (8.7 million), Malaysia (7.9 million), Singapore (6.9 million), and Indonesia (4.3 million). > This bill seeks to address these issues by creating the position of tourism officer in all provinces, first class municipalities and cities, or municipalities and cities where tourism is considered a major local industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2002-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIE S, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The continuous degradation of our environment is somehow a result of government neglect. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources, while attending to problems concerning our forests and natural resources, had neglected the environment. We do not even have concrete standards on air, water and land quality. More so, we lack strageties and action plans to safeguard public health against poor environmental quality. What this nation therefore needs is a separate goverment entity which will focus on environmental concerns such as air and water pollution, solid and toxic wastes, hazardous substances, and public health. > This bill proposes the creation of the Naitonal Environmental Management Authority (NEMA), an environmenttal watchdog which shall be responsible for the conservation of the country's environment and resources, regulation of environmental impact occasioned by human activities, and control and abatement of enviromental pollution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2002-08-05

rows.abstract: Rationale: Gambling has gone beyond the control of government law enforcement agencies as shown by the proliferation of jueteng and other illegal gambling games that have permeated even far-flung areas of the country. Decades of proliferation in thecountry of jueteng, as a primary example, has become a systematic social dilemma as it has been observed that the significant stakeholders in this illegal numbers game are mostly from the poor or those who belong in the lower strata. > This bill seeks to increase the penalties for those involved in illegal gambling to include not only the participants and the operators but government officials concerned with the full implementation of this Act. More importantly the bill provides for a penalty oof both imprisonment and fine for those found to be involved in illegal gambling. rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2002-08-07

rows.abstract: Rationale: The past decade witnessed the growth and expansion of Rehabilitation Medicine as a specialty in the medical field. For one, the number of trainees, graduates, certififed diplomates and fellows has increased tremendously. rows.abstract: Rationale: At present, school district supervisors are inadequately compensated, considering that in general, before they become as such, they have to go through the rigid administrative processes and experience first as a teacher, and later as a school principal. Technically, the salary grade of a district supervisor is salary grade (SG) - 19, while that of a secondary school principal is SG - 21, or to steps higher. > This billseeks to ensure that schools district supervisors are commensurately compensated. rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE GENERAL GUIDELINES IN THE SALE, REQUALIFICATION , DISTRIBUTION, AND REPAIR OF LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) CYLINDERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "LPG Cylinder Act of 2002". This bill substantiates the policy of the State to: (1) Ensure that appropriate standards will be developed and formulated for the LPG sector through the coordinated efforts of DTI, other government agencies, and the private sector; (2) Provide for the penalties and fines for the violation of this Act; (3) Promote awareness and educate all sectors of society regarding the safety requirements and proper use of LPG cylinders; and (4) Formulate and implement a comprehensive program that shall promote national consciousness to ensure consumer protection.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06503

rows.author: D001
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING UNLAWFUL FOR FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS AND OTHER ENTITIES ENGAGED IN CREDIT CARD BUSINESS TO CHARGE INTEREST RATES EXCEEDING FORTY-TWO PERCENT (42%) PER ANNUM, INCLUDING PENALTY FOR LATE PAYMENT AND OTHER FINANCE CHARGES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: It is hereby declared unlawful for financial establishments and other entities engaged in credit card business to charge interest rates exceeding forty two percent (42%) per annum, including penalty for late payment and other finance charges. As used in this Act, the term "credit card" refers to any card, plate, code coupon book or other credit device that can be used to obtain money, goods, property, services or any other thing of value. > Any person found guilty of violating the provision ofthis Act shall suffer the penalty of not less than three (3) years nor more than six (6) years or a fine of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00) or both at the discretion of the court. If the offender is a corporation, the penalty and/or fine shaall be imposed upon the president, director and manager or managing partners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2002-08-14

rows.author: D001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING GOVERNMENT SUBSIDY TO FARMERS' IRRIGATION FEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3601, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to grant a government subsidy to farmers by deducting an amount equivalent to fifty percent (50%) from the total irrigation fees or administration charges. It is the primordial concern of this measure to provide a lasting solution acceptable and beneficial to both the government and the farmers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2002-08-14

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF BALLET IN THE PRIMARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS OF EDUCATION
rows.abstract: Ballet shall be taught in all public and private elementary ang high schools in the Philippines, The teaching of ballet as a topic in Physical Education shall include its history, development and growth.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997, AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6657, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW OF 1988
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to exempt the interest earnings of Landbank of the Philippines (LBP) bonds paid by the government to landowners for land acquisition under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Act of 1988, from the 20% withholding tax imposed by the National Internal Revenue Code.

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2002-08-14

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM WITHHOLDING TAX THE INTEREST EARNINGS ON BONDS ISSUED BY THE LANDBANK OF THE PHILIPPINES TO LANDOWNERS ON THE SALE OF THEIR LANDS COVERED BY THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROTECTING THE RIGHTS TO LABOR OF THE WORKERS OF INTERNATIONAL RICE RESEARCH INSTITUTE (IRRI) AS ENSHRINED IN THE 1987 CONSTITUTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 3 OF THE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1620, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Protecting the Rights to Labor of Workers of International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to ensure the protection of the basic rights of the workers of the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI). The bill once enacted into law will correct an injustice done to the workers who have been deprived of their labor rights since the signing of the Marcos edict on 19 April 1979 which granted IRRI immunity from any penal, civil and administrative proceedings.
rows.status: Bill reported out 2003-04-28 (#01394);Submitted by LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT

rows.author: D072
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE OFFENSE OF PRESENTING TO THE PUBLIC SUSPECTS WHO ARE WRONGFULLY ACCUSED WITHOUT DUE PROCESS
rows.abstract: "Anti-False Witness Act." This bill seeks to punish erring government officials who label persons as suspsects to an offense or crime, even if they have not yet been formally charged by the courts. It is high time that the perpetrators of such a system of "swift justice" should pay the price of putting innocent persons in the hot seat and permanently destorying their name and dignity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2002-08-14

rows.author: C112
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO SET ASIDE THE FORTY PERCENT (40%) SHARE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FROM THE VALUE-ADDED TAX (VAT) COLLECTED BY THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS (BOC) FOR THE BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE (BIR) TO AUGMENT THE FUNDING EXCLUSIVELY FOR BASIC HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND FACILITIES DEVOLVED TO PROVINCES AND HIGHLY URBANIZED CITIES
rows.abstract: The forty percent (40%) share of local government units from the Value Added Tax (VAT) collected by the Bureau of Customs  for the Bureau of Internal Revenue is hereby set aside to augment the funding exclusively for basic health care services and facilities devolved to provinces and highly urbanized cities.> The share of each provice or higly urbanized city, with devolved health care services and facilities, shall be distributed equitably on the basis of population within its territorial jurisdiction.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2002-08-14

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTIES FOR THE OFFENSE OF BRIBERY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 210, 211 AND 212 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: Bribery is the most pervasive form of graft and corruption praticed by public officers in the course of official duties. As defined, it is the act of offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting of any thing of value to influence action asan official or in discharge of legal or public duty. > This bill seeks to amend Articles 210, 211 and 212 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended, by increasing the imposable penalties for the crime of bribery.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2002-08-14

rows.author: B004

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLITICAL PARTY SYSTEM
rows.abstract: "Political Party Act of 2002". Rationale: It is imperative that political party system should be strengthened if we want to develop achieve genuine political development and democratization . We have to enact laws to prevent the system of ward politics and political chameleons that we have today.> This bill envisions to change the norm of having political butterflies during and after the election period.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06418

rows.author: D063
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A TEN PERCENT (10%) EXCISE TAX ON PREPAID CARDS BY PROVIDING A NEW SECTION, SECTION 149-A, AMENDING CHAPTER VI OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: A new Section 149-A is added to the National Internal Revenue code, and shall read as follows: THERE SHALL BE LEVIED, ASSESSED AND COLLECTED A TEN PERCENT (10%) AD VALOREM TAX ON ALL PREPAID CARDS BASED ON THE VALUE OR DENOMINATION AT THE FACE OF THE CARD, NET OF THE EXCISE AND THE VALUE-ADDED TAX. > A PREPAID CARD IS DEFINED IN THIS ACT AS A CARD WHICH HAS ON ITS FACE, A VALUE OR DENOMINATION AND IS USED AS A DEVISE IR A MODE FOR PAYING THE SERVICES TO BE RENDERED BY THE TELECOMMUNICATI ON COMPANIES, INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS, TRANSPORTATION COMPANIES, OR ANY OTHER COMPANY USING PREPAID CARDS FOR ITS SERVICES.> PROVIDED, THAT EACH CARD SHALL HAVE A BAR CODE AFFIXED ON A CONSPICUOUS PLACE IN THE CARD BEFORE ANY REMOVAL FROM THE PREMISES OOF THE MANUFACTURER OF SUCH PREPAID CARDS CAN BE MADE. THE AFFIXTURE MUST BE DONE IN SUCH  A MANNER THAT WILL PREVENT SAID BAR CODE FROM BEING REMOVED OR ERASED BY WASHING OR ANY OTHER MEANS AND FROM COVERING ANY WARNING THAT MAY BE HEREAFTER REQUIRE
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2002-08-20
